plan.topic: Is your semaglutide pen real? What the FDA has said about counterfeit Ozempic pens and what to check
plan.angle: Title: 'Is Your Semaglutide Pen Real? What the FDA Flagged #shorts'. Answer within 10 s: 'The FDA has warned three times, most recently in December 2025, about counterfeit Ozempic found in the US supply chain.' Then the Dec 2025 detail exactly as the FDA wrote it: counterfeit 1 mg pens labelled lot PAR1229, which is also a real lot, so check where the EXP/LOT text sits. On the fake it's to the left of the date and lot, not above. One line: earlier FDA alerts named lots NAR0074 (2023) and PAR0362 (2025), with full details at FDA.gov. FDA advice: get it with a prescription from a state-licensed pharmacy, and report suspected fakes to FDA MedWatch. 'Don't stop or change your medicine on your own; ask your pharmacist or prescriber.' Full prescriber line. Last spoken line: 'Full breakdown: [L1's exact published title], on our channel.' L1's video URL goes in the pinned comment and on description line 1. No seller names, no emoji, 170 words or fewer.
plan.working_title: Is Your Semaglutide Pen Real? What the FDA Flagged #shorts
plan.why: Spin-off of L1. It names a drug, adds FDA counterfeit-pen facts our 10-17 Short didn't cover, and sends viewers to today's long-form. | fact-check: Facts confirmed on fda.gov. There are three FDA counterfeit Ozempic warnings: Dec 2023 (lot NAR0074, serial 430834149057; needles also counterfeit, so sterility can't be confirmed), Apr 2025 (lot PAR0362, serials starting 51746517) and Dec 2025 (counterfeit 1 mg seized in the legitimate US supply chain, lot PAR1229, which is also a real lot number; on the fake, the 'EXP/LOT' text is to the left of the date and lot instead of above). Fitting all three lot and serial sets into 170 words risks wrong numbers on screen. Lead with the most recent (Dec 2025) alert and mention that earlier alerts exist. Each alert needs its own FDA page URL, not an index page. Sticking to the FDA's own 'check your pen' instructions is fine. Don't present the lot or serial check as proof that a pen is genuine, because the FDA says PAR1229 is also an authentic lot. The CTA title must exactly match L1's final published title, and S3 can only run if L1 actually goes live at 14:00. Otherwise say 'follow for more'.

package.description:
Is your Ozempic (semaglutide) pen real? FDA has updated its counterfeit Ozempic warning three times for the US supply chain, most recently Dec 5, 2025, flagging fake 1 mg pens on lot PAR1229 — a lot that's also genuine, so the number alone proves nothing. FDA's clue: "EXP/LOT" sits left of the date and lot on the fakes, not above it like on genuine pens.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you. Don't stop or change your treatment on your own.

factcheck.summary: I checked every claim against the live FDA alert (S1) and the FDA Counterfeit Medicine page (S3), and both say what the script says. The page has three updates (12/21/2023, 4/14/2025 and 12/5/2025), and the latest is still 12/5/2025. All three cover Ozempic 1 mg. The identifiers match exactly: NAR0074 with serial 430834149057, PAR0362 with serials starting 51746517, and PAR1229. The label clue is right too: on the fakes, the EXP/LOT text sits to the left of the date and lot, while on genuine pens it sits above. FDA also says PAR1229 pens received through Novo Nordisk's Patient Assistance Program are authentic and can still be used. The prescription and state-licensed pharmacy advice is verbatim. Side effects go to MedWatch, and suspected fakes can be reported to FDA (the consumer complaint coordinator or the Office of Criminal Investigations, as S3 says). Nothing is invented, and the dates and numbers are correct. The safety framing works: it separates "don't use a suspected fake" from "don't stop treatment on your own", and it includes the disclaimer and the prescriber line. Three small wording fixes would tighten the muted-viewer reading and how the advice is credited. None of them blocks shipping.

hold_reason: Dropped by Editor-in-Chief: The facts check out, but the subtitle text is wrong where it counts. The ASR heard the correct words, so the errors are in the subtitles: they say "pin"/"pins" instead of "pen"/"pens" and "fiveth" instead of "fifth", and they render the key lot number PAR1229 as "parone thousand two hundred twenty". In a Short about spotting counterfeit pens, a garbled or wrong lot number on screen could mislead viewers, so this needs new captions built from the script's on-screen text (PAR1229, Dec 5, 2025) before it ships.
